observations.statement: The core defines seven UI elements on the Source Control surface and binds each exact command ID to an exact handlers::git target: worktree, compare, create, focus_lineage, list, lock, and open. Every entry declares an empty expected_event_types array.

Every command must be registered in the UICommand dispatcher with typed arguments and a result contract, expose projected availability and a disabled reason before dispatch, preserve command_id, origin, correlation_id, handler target, result, and an effect in dispatch evidence, and declare its production-certification contract.

Each entry names a command-specific availability selector, disabled-reason projection, receipt effect, and dispatch_receipt reference; each effect description requires an explicit no-persist receipt or route/open disposition and rejects placeholder command_applied events.

Production certification for each command explicitly requires render/control evidence, a dispatcher fixture, a typed payload/result assertion, projected-state and disabled-reason proof, a receipt/event assertion, an accessibility check, and regression-test evidence.

Each accessibility contract requires stable role/name/description semantics matching its command, keyboard reachability and activation when visible, visible focus with deterministic return after dispatch or error, and assistive-technology announcement of the command-specific disabled reason.
Each event-test requirement demands its named dispatch receipt or an explicit route/open disposition and asserts that no unexpected persisted domain event is emitted.

candidate_findings.title: Typed payload and result contracts are required but undefined
candidate_findings.statement: All seven entries demand typed arguments, payloads, and results, but the assigned core supplies no field names, field types, required-versus-optional rules, validation constraints, result variants, or serialization contract for any command.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can produce mutually incompatible dispatcher APIs while still claiming the generic requirement, and certification cannot assert an exact payload or result shape.

candidate_findings.title: Command-specific behavior and success outcomes are unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The entries identify controls, command IDs, handlers, selectors, and generic receipt evidence, but do not define the operation performed by worktree, compare, create, focus_lineage, list, lock, or open, their command-specific prerequisites, their output meaning, or their observable success conditions.
candidate_findings.impact: The same wiring contract permits materially different product behavior and handler results for each named capability.

candidate_findings.title: The route/open alternative conflicts with unconditional typed-contract language
candidate_findings.statement: Each first acceptance check unconditionally requires a typed args/result contract, while a later check permits either a typed payload/result contract or an explicit route/open no-persist disposition; the core does not state whether the disposition alternative waives any typed contract or how the two checks are reconciled.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations and certification tests can disagree on whether route/open commands require typed arguments and results.

candidate_findings.title: Receipt versus route/open disposition branching lacks a contract
candidate_findings.statement: Each effect is labeled receipt and names one dispatch_receipt reference, yet both the effect description and event test allow an explicit route/open disposition without defining the selection condition, disposition fields, status model, consumer, or relationship to success and failure.
candidate_findings.impact: Handlers can choose different effect paths and emit incompatible evidence for equivalent executions.

candidate_findings.title: Availability and disabled-reason state are path-only contracts
candidate_findings.statement: The core names availability and disabled-reason projection paths but does not define their value types, valid states, derivation authority, update triggers, transition timing, stale or loading behavior, or atomic consistency relationship.
candidate_findings.impact: Controls and assistive technology may expose inconsistent enabled state and disabled explanations around dispatch and state changes.

candidate_findings.title: Failure and execution-lifecycle semantics are absent
candidate_findings.statement: The contracts mention dispatch, result, and focus return after error, but do not define error categories, error representation, whether failures produce receipts or dispositions, timeout, cancellation, retry, ordering, concurrency, or idempotency behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Duplicate actions, racing state, cancellation, and handler failures can be handled inconsistently without violating any exact requirement in the window.

candidate_findings.title: Accessibility values and focus destination remain builder-defined
candidate_findings.statement: The accessibility clauses require a stable role/name/description matching the command, keyboard operation where visible, and deterministic focus return, but do not specify the exact semantic role, accessible name or description, visibility predicate, or focus destination after success and error.
candidate_findings.impact: Different controls can pass the prose-level requirement while exposing divergent keyboard and assistive-technology behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Event-effect language is unresolved against the empty event contract
candidate_findings.statement: Every entry declares expected_event_types as empty and its event test rejects unexpected persisted domain events, while acceptance and certification language still permits a receipt or event effect and a receipt/event assertion; the core does not define whether any non-persisted event effect is valid.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders and test authors can disagree on whether an event-based effect is conformant and which event, if any, may be observed.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: UI location, UI element identity, command identity, handler target, and the absence of expected event types are explicit for all seven core entries.
Each command has an explicit availability selector path and disabled-reason projection path.
Each command has an explicit dispatch_receipt reference, rejects placeholder command_applied events, and has an event-test oracle that forbids unexpected persisted domain events.
The window explicitly covers role/name/description semantics, keyboard activation, focus handling, and disabled-state announcement for every control.
The production-certification evidence categories and required dispatch-evidence metadata fields are explicitly enumerated for every command.

unknowns.statement: The exact argument and result schemas, validation rules, and result variants for all seven commands cannot be determined from the assigned core.
The exact command-specific operation, prerequisite model, success output, and user-visible success or failure outcome cannot be determined from the assigned core.
The authority that derives and updates each availability and disabled-reason projection, and the projections' state-transition model, cannot be determined from the assigned core.
The condition for choosing a dispatch receipt versus a route/open disposition, and the disposition's exact schema and consumer, cannot be determined from the assigned core.
Retry, cancellation, timeout, ordering, concurrency, and idempotency behavior cannot be determined from the assigned core.
The exact accessible role, name, description, visibility predicate, and post-dispatch or post-error focus target cannot be determined from the assigned core.
Whether any non-persisted event effect is permitted despite expected_event_types being empty cannot be determined from the assigned core.
